CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: DOM-based XSS through attacker-supplied filenames; security severity MEDIUM, confidence 9/10. handleFiles interpolates file.name into validation-error strings at lines 73-75; showErrors at lines 215-218 inserts these strings using innerHTML without escaping. A file named '.txt' triggers the unsupported-type error and is parsed as HTML, causing its event handler to run in the application's origin. An attacker must persuade a victim to select or drop an attacker-named file; exploitation does not require successful upload or backend authentication. Separately, upload response originalFileName values are interpolated into attributes and HTML text at lines 185-189, then parsed by insertAdjacentHTML at line 157. HomeController.uploadPhotos returns the original multipart filename at line 77. No escaping guard or CSP configuration was identified for these DOM sinks. The client-validation path demonstrates the vulnerability without assuming that another visitor's server-rendered gallery executes stored filenames; server-rendered Thymeleaf text is escaped.
